Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.

Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior

# Crowbook

Crowbook lets you write a book in Markdown and generate HTML, PDF and EPUB output without worrying about formatting or typography.

It focuses on novels and fiction and provides sensible defaults to produce readable books with correct typography.

## Example

To see Crowbook's output examples, see the project's published book pages (HTML, PDF, EPUB) on the project's website or releases.

## Installing

Download a precompiled binary for your platform from the project's releases page and place the executable somewhere on your PATH.

## Usage

The simplest invocation is:

    $ crowbook <BOOK>

where <BOOK> is a book configuration file. Crowbook will parse this file and generate HTML, EPUB, and/or PDF output according to the settings.

For short texts contained in a single Markdown file, Crowbook can accept a single Markdown file with embedded metadata and produce output directly.

## Output formats

Crowbook supports HTML, PDF and EPUB as output formats.

Note: Generating PDF output typically requires a working LaTeX installation (for example, xelatex) on your system.

## Input format

Crowbook accepts CommonMark-like Markdown input. You can also include a small metadata block (YAML) at the top of a single Markdown file to set title/author and other options when running in single-file mode.

## Customization

Templates allow you to customize the visual appearance of the generated books. See the project's documentation for template usage and examples.

## Bugs and support

Report issues on the project's issue tracker (link available on the project's website or GitHub repository page).

  -q, --quiet

    font-weight: bold;
    margin-right: 1em;
}

td.note-number {
    vertical-align: top;
}

/* When footnotes (try to) be displayed as margin notes */
.sidenote {
    display: block;
    float: right;
    width: 30%;
    border: 1px solid black;
    margin: 1em;
    padding: .5em;
    margin-right: -1.5em;
}

.sidenote .note-number {
    float: left;
}

/* The div class displaying notes at the end of a chapter */
div.notes {
    text-align: justify;
    border-top: thin dashed black;
    margin-top: 1em;
}

table.notes {
    border-collapse: collapse;
    border-style: hidden;
}

table.notes tr td {
    margin-left: 1em;
    margin-right: 1em;
}

table.notes tr td p {
    text-indent: 0;
}
                 
/* Every markdown table is included in a <div class = "table"> */
.table {
    margin: 1em;
}

.table table {
    width: 80%;
    margin: 0 auto;
    border-style: solid;
    border-width: thin;
    border-color: black;
    border-collapse: collapse;
}

.table table th, .table table td {
    border-style: solid;
    border-width: 1px;
    text-align: center;
}

.table table th {
    font-weight: bold;
    font-variant: small-caps;
}

function remove_footnotes() {
    var footnotes = document.querySelectorAll('.popup_footnote');
    for (var i = 0; i < footnotes.length; i++) {
        var f = footnotes[i];
        if (f.parentNode) {
            f.parentNode.removeChild(f);
        }
    }
}

function show_footnote(event) {
    remove_footnotes();
    var id = event.target.getAttribute("id");
    var target_id = id.replace("source", "dest");
    var content = document.getElementById(target_id).innerHTML;
    var top = Math.round(event.target.getBoundingClientRect().top + event.target.getBoundingClientRect().height);
    event.target.insertAdjacentHTML('afterend', '<aside class = "popup_footnote" style = "position: fixed; top: '+ top + 'px; ">' + content + '</aside>')
}

{"command":"python3 <<'PY'
import subprocess, os, tempfile, re
tmp=tempfile.mkdtemp()
# More book lang tests: check TOC title, etc.
for blang in ["en","fr","es","de"]:
    open(os.path.join(tmp,"a.md"),"w").write("# Ch1\n\nC1\n")
    open(os.path.join(tmp,"b.md"),"w").write("# Ch2\n\nC2\n")
    open(os.path.join(tmp,"b.book"),"w").write("title: T\nlang: "+blang+"\noutput.html: out.html\n\n+ a.md\n+ b.md\n")
    try: os.remove(os.path.join(tmp,"out.html"))
    except: pass
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","b.book"], cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True)
    html=open(os.path.join(tmp,"out.html")).read() if os.path.exists(os.path.join(tmp,"out.html")) else ""
    # Find TOC? nav
    nav = html[html.find('<nav'):html.find('</nav>')+6] if '<nav' in html else "no nav"
    # Find menu alt/title (loc_toc)
    m=re.search(r'alt = "(.*?)" title', html)
    alt = m.group(1) if m else "?"
    print("lang",blang,"alt",alt)
    print(nav[:800])
    print("---")
PY
"}

    font-family: Linux Biolinum, sans-serif;
    font-variant: small-caps;
}

/* Title of a part */
h1.part {
    font-size: 250%;
    text-align: center;
}

/* The `Part X` section of a part */
h2.part {
    font-size: 175%;
    text-align: center;
}

/* The "Chapter X" section of a chapter */
span.chapter-header {
    font-size: 75%;
}

/* Title of the book */
h1.title {
    text-align: center;
    font-size: 300%;
}
/* Author */
h2.author {
    text-align: right;
    font-size:  200%;
}

/* Subtitle */
h2.subtitle {
    text-align: center;
    font-size: 200%;
}

/* When toc is displayed inlined */
#toc ol, #toc ul {
    padding: 0;
    margin-left: 1em;
}
#toc li {
    list-style-type: none;
    margin: 0; padding: 0;
}

#toc li:before {
    content: none;
}

#cover img {
    width: 100%;
    max-height: 100%;
}

.image {
    margin: auto;
    width: 80%;
}

.image img {
    width: 100%;
    max-height: 100%;
}

.rule {
    text-align: center !important;
    margin-top: 1em;
    margin-bottom: 1em;
    font-weight: bold;
    page-break-inside: avoid;
    break-inside: avoid;
    page-break-after: avoid;
    break-after: avoid;
}

/* The number of the note in an expanded footnote (e.g. [3]) */
.note-number {
    font-weight: bold;
    margin-right: 1em;
}

td.note-number {
    vertical-align: top;
}

/* When footnotes (try to) be displayed as margin notes */
.sidenote {
    display: block;
    float: right;
    width: 30%;
    border: 1px solid black;
    margin: 1em;
    padding: .5em;
    margin-right: -1.5em;
}

.sidenote .note-number {
    float: left;
}

/* The div class displaying notes at the end of a chapter */
div.notes {
    text-align: justify;
    border-top: thin dashed black;
    margin-top: 1em;
}

table.notes {
    border-collapse: collapse;
    border-style: hidden;
}

table.notes tr td {
    margin-left: 1em;
    margin-right: 1em;
}

table.notes tr td p {
    text-indent: 0;
}
                 
/* Every markdown table is included in a <div class = "table"> */
.table {
    margin: 1em;
}

.table table {
    width: 80%;
    margin: 0 auto;
    border-style: solid;
    border-width: thin;
    border-color: black;
    border-collapse: collapse;
}

.table table th, .table table td {
    border-style: solid;
    border-width: 1px;
    text-align: center;
}

.table table th {
    font-weight: bold;
    font-variant: small-caps;
}



span.initial {

p.first-para {

# Crowbook

Crowbook lets you write a book in Markdown and generate HTML, PDF and EPUB output without worrying about formatting or typography.

It focuses on novels and fiction and provides sensible defaults to produce readable books with correct typography.

## Example

To see Crowbook's output examples, see the project's published book pages (HTML, PDF, EPUB) on the project's website or releases.

## Installing

Download a precompiled binary for your platform from the project's releases page and place the executable somewhere on your PATH.

## Usage

The simplest invocation is:

    $ crowbook <BOOK>

where <BOOK> is a book configuration file. Crowbook will parse this file and generate HTML, EPUB, and/or PDF output according to the settings.

For short texts contained in a single Markdown file, Crowbook can accept a single Markdown file with embedded metadata and produce output directly.

## Output formats

Crowbook supports HTML, PDF and EPUB as output formats.

Note: Generating PDF output typically requires a working LaTeX installation (for example, xelatex) on your system.

## Input format

Crowbook accepts CommonMark-like Markdown input. You can also include a small metadata block (YAML) at the top of a single Markdown file to set title/author and other options when running in single-file mode.

## Customization

Templates allow you to customize the visual appearance of the generated books. See the project's documentation for template usage and examples.

## Bugs and support

Report issues on the project's issue tracker (link available on the project's website or GitHub repository page).

def parse_cli(argv):
    # argv is sys.argv[1:]
    pn = prog_name()
    # First, check help/version (before validation)
    # Scan in order, handling combined shorts
    # Returns None if no help/version, else exits
    # We need to handle --help/--version with = as errors, not help
    # So scan for exact --help/-h/--version/-V before --
    # For combined shorts, check chars in order
    def scan_help_version(args):
        first = None  # 'help' or 'version'
        for a in args:
            if a == "--":
                break
            if a == "--help":
                if first is None:
                    first = 'help'
                break  # first wins, no need to continue? Actually need to find first, so break at first found
            elif a == "--version":
                if first is None:
                    first = 'version'
                break
            elif a.startswith("--help=") or a.startswith("--version="):
                # These are errors, not help/version. But do they override? No, they will error later.
                # However, if there's also a valid help before, help wins? Since we break at first valid, and these are not valid, continue.
                continue
            elif a.startswith("--"):
                continue
            elif a.startswith("-") and len(a) >= 2 and a != "-":
                # short(s)
                # Handle -h/-V with attached? -hfoo => help, -Vfoo => version
                # Iterate chars
                chars = a[1:]
                # Need to handle value-taking shorts: o,t,L,c consume rest as value, so h/V after them are part of value, not flags
                # e.g., -oV? That's -o with value V, not -V. Similarly -th? -t with value h.
                # So iterate, and if char is o/t/L/c, break (rest is value)
                for ch in chars:
                    if ch in ('o','t','L','c'):
                        break
                    elif ch == 'h':
                        if first is None:
                            first = 'help'
                        break
                    elif ch == 'V':
                        if first is None:

        else:

def tex_escape(s):
    ph="\x00BSLASH\x00"
    s=s.replace('\\',ph)
    s=s.replace('{',r'\{').replace('}',r'\}')
    s=s.replace('%',r'\%').replace('$',r'\$').replace('&',r'\&').replace('#',r'\#').replace('_',r'\_')
    s=s.replace('~',r'\~{}').replace('^',r'\^{}')
    s=s.replace(ph,r'\textbackslash{}')
    return s

        src=mt.group(1)
        if re.match(r'^(https?://|data:|ftp://)',src):
            return f"\\mdimage{{{tex_escape(src)}}}"
        img_base=options.get('resources.base_path.images','.')
        base_for_img=options.get('resources.base_path',None)
        img_dir=base_for_img if base_for_img else (img_base if img_base is not None else ".")
        bdir=base_dir
        if os.path.isabs(src):
            cp=src; dp=src
        else:
            if img_dir in (".","./",""):
                if bdir in (".","","./"):
                    cp=os.path.join(".",src); dp=os.path.join(".",src)
                else:
                    cp=os.path.join(bdir,src); dp=os.path.join(bdir,src)
            else:
                cp=os.path.join(img_dir,src); dp=os.path.join(img_dir,src)
        if not os.path.isfile(cp):

    s=s.replace('\\',ph)
    s=s.replace('{',r'\{').replace('}',r'\}')
    s=s.replace('%',r'\%').replace('$',r'\$').replace('&',r'\&').replace('#',r'\#').replace('_',r'\_')
    s=s.replace('~',r'\~{}').replace('^',r'\^{}')
    s=s.replace(ph,r'\textbackslash{}')
    return s

def format_stats(file_stats, total_chars, total_words):
    max_fn=max([len(fn) for fn,_,_ in file_stats]) if file_stats else 0
    header="Chapter"+" "*max_fn+"Chars      Words  Chars/Word"
    lines=[header,"---------"]
    for fn,ch,wo in file_stats:
        if wo==0:
            avg_str="NaN" if ch==0 else "inf"
        else:
            avg_str=f"{ch/wo:.2f}"
        gap1=11-(len(str(ch))-1)+(max_fn-len(fn))
        gap2=10-(len(str(wo))-1)
        gap3=8-(len(avg_str)-4)
        gap1=max(1,gap1); gap2=max(1,gap2); gap3=max(1,gap3)
        lines.append(f"{fn}{' '*gap1}{ch}{' '*gap2}{wo}{' '*gap3}{avg_str}")
    lines.append("---------")
    if total_words==0:
        total_avg="NaN" if total_chars==0 else "inf"
    else:
        total_avg=f"{total_chars/total_words:.2f}"
    gap1_t=11-(len(str(total_chars))-1)+(max_fn-len("TOTAL:"))
    gap2_t=10-(len(str(total_words))-1)
    gap3_t=8-(len(total_avg)-4)
    gap1_t=max(1,gap1_t); gap2_t=max(1,gap2_t); gap3_t=max(1,gap3_t)
    lines.append(f"TOTAL:{' '*gap1_t}{total_chars}{' '*gap2_t}{total_words}{' '*gap3_t}{total_avg}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def simple_stats_count(md_text, options):
    lines=md_text.splitlines()
    filt=[]
    for ln in lines:
        if re.match(r'^\[\^([^\]]+?)\]:',ln.strip()):
            continue
        filt.append(ln)
    blocks=[]
    cur=[]
    for ln in filt:
        if ln.strip()=="":
            if cur:
                blocks.append("\n".join(cur))
                cur=[]
        else:
            cur.append(ln)
    if cur:
        blocks.append("\n".join(cur))
    block_texts=[]
    for b in blocks:
        blines=b.split("\n")
        if len(blines)>=2 and '|' in blines[0] and re.match(r'^\s*\|?[\s:\-|]+\|?\s*$',blines[1]) and '-' in blines[1]:
            continue
        if len(blines)==1:
            s0=blines[0].strip()
            nospace=s0.replace(' ','').replace('\t','')
            if len(nospace)>=3 and all(c==nospace[0] for c in nospace) and nospace[0] in ('*','-','_'):
                continue
        if len(blines)>=2 and blines[0].lstrip().startswith('```') and blines[-1].strip().startswith('```'):
            middle=blines[1:-1]
            ct=" ".join([l.strip() for l in middle])
            block_texts.append(ct.strip())
            continue
        is_ind=False
        for ln in blines:
            if ln.strip()=="" :
                continue
            if not ln.startswith('    '):
                is_ind=False
                break
        else:
            is_ind=True
        # Actually above loop logic wrong (for-else with break? Simplify: check all non-blank start with 4 spaces)
        is_ind2=True
        for ln in blines:
            if ln.strip()=="":
                continue
            if not ln.startswith('    '):
                is_ind2=False
                break
        if is_ind2 and len(blines)>=1:
            stripped=[ln[4:] if ln.startswith('    ') else ln for ln in blines]
            ct2=" ".join([l.strip() for l in stripped if l.strip()!=""])
            block_texts.append(ct2.strip())
            continue
        cleaned=[]
        for ln in blines:
            ln2=re.sub(r'^ {0,3}#{1,6}\s+','',ln)
            ln2=re.sub(r'^\s*>\s?','',ln2)
            ln2=re.sub(r'^\s*[-*+]\s+','',ln2)
            ln2=re.sub(r'^\s*\d+[.)]\s+','',ln2)
            ln2=re.sub(r'^\[[ xX]\]\s+','',ln2)
            cleaned.append(ln2)
        if len(cleaned)==2 and cleaned[1].lstrip().startswith(':'):
            term=cleaned[0].strip()
            defi=re.sub(r'^:\s*','',cleaned[1].strip())
            block_joined=term+defi
        else:
            block_joined=" ".join([l.strip() for l in cleaned])
        t=block_joined
        t=re.sub(r'!\[[^\]]*?\]\([^\)]+?\)','',t)
        t=re.sub(r'\[([^\]]*?)\]\([^\)]+?\)',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'`([^`\n]+?)`',r'\1',t)
        sup_en=options.get('crowbook.markdown.superscript',False)
        if sup_en:
            t=re.sub(r'~~([^~\n]+?)~~',r'\1',t)
            t=re.sub(r'~([^~\n]+?)~',r'\1',t)
            t=re.sub(r'\^([^\^\n]+?)\^',r'\1',t)
        else:
            t=re.sub(r'~~([^~\n]+?)~~',r'\1',t)
            t=re.sub(r'~([^~\n]+?)~',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'\*\*([^\*\n]+?)\*\*',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'__([^_\n]+?)__',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'\*([^\*\n]+?)\*',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'_([^_\n]+?)_',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'<((?:https?://|ftp://)[^<>\s]+?)>',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'\\(.)',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'\[\^([^\]]+?)\]','',t)
        block_texts.append(t)
    joined="".join(block_texts)
    chars=len(joined)
    words=len(joined.split()) if joined.strip()!="" else 0
    return chars,words

def format_stats(file_stats, total_chars, total_words):
    max_fn=max([len(fn) for fn,_,_ in file_stats]) if file_stats else 0
    header="Chapter"+" "*max_fn+"Chars      Words  Chars/Word"
    lines=[header,"---------"]
    for fn,ch,wo in file_stats:
        if wo==0:
            avg_str="NaN" if ch==0 else "inf"
        else:
            avg_str=f"{ch/wo:.2f}"
        gap1=11-(len(str(ch))-1)+(max_fn-len(fn))
        gap2=10-(len(str(wo))-1)
        gap3=8-(len(avg_str)-4)
        gap1=max(1,gap1); gap2=max(1,gap2); gap3=max(1,gap3)
        lines.append(f"{fn}{' '*gap1}{ch}{' '*gap2}{wo}{' '*gap3}{avg_str}")
    lines.append("---------")
    if total_words==0:
        total_avg="NaN" if total_chars==0 else "inf"
    else:
        total_avg=f"{total_chars/total_words:.2f}"
    gap1_t=11-(len(str(total_chars))-1)+(max_fn-len("TOTAL:"))
    gap2_t=10-(len(str(total_words))-1)
    gap3_t=8-(len(total_avg)-4)
    gap1_t=max(1,gap1_t); gap2_t=max(1,gap2_t); gap3_t=max(1,gap3_t)
    lines.append(f"TOTAL:{' '*gap1_t}{total_chars}{' '*gap2_t}{total_words}{' '*gap3_t}{total_avg}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def tex_escape(s):
    ph="\x00BSLASH\x00"
    s=s.replace('\\',ph)
    s=s.replace('{',r'\{').replace('}',r'\}')
    s=s.replace('%',r'\%').replace('$',r'\$').replace('&',r'\&').replace('#',r'\#').replace('_',r'\_')
    s=s.replace('~',r'\~{}').replace('^',r'\^{}')
    s=s.replace(ph,r'\textbackslash{}')
    return s
def parse_inline_tex(text, options, base_dir=".", md_path="c.md", runtime_lang='en'):
    errors=[]
    placeholders={}; ph_id=0
    def ph_rep(m):
        nonlocal ph_id
        cc=m.group(1)
        esc=tex_escape(cc)
        k=f"\x00TCODE{ph_id}\x00"
        placeholders[k]=f"\\mdcode{{{esc}}}"

            middle=blines[1:-1]

        is_ind2=True

            if not ln.startswith('    '):

        cleaned=[]

    max_fn=max([len(fn) for fn,_,_ in file_stats]) if file_stats else 0
    header="Chapter"+" "*max_fn+"Chars      Words  Chars/Word"
    lines=[header,"---------"]
    for fn,ch,wo in file_stats:
        if wo==0:
            avg_str="NaN" if ch==0 else "inf"

        gap1=11-(len(str(ch))-1)+(max_fn-len(fn))

        gap1=max(1,gap1); gap2=max(1,gap2); gap3=max(1,gap3)
        lines.append(f"{fn}{' '*gap1}{ch}{' '*gap2}{wo}{' '*gap3}{avg_str}")
    lines.append("---------")
    if total_words==0:
        total_avg="NaN" if total_chars==0 else "inf"

def simple_stats_count(md_text, options):
    lines=md_text.splitlines()
    filt=[]
    for ln in lines:
        if re.match(r'^\[\^([^\]]+?)\]:',ln.strip()):
            continue
        filt.append(ln)
    blocks=[]
    cur=[]
    for ln in filt:
        if ln.strip()=="":
            if cur:
                blocks.append("\n".join(cur))
                cur=[]
        else:
            cur.append(ln)
    if cur:
        blocks.append("\n".join(cur))
    block_texts=[]
    for b in blocks:
        blines=b.split("\n")
        if len(blines)>=2 and '|' in blines[0] and re.match(r'^\s*\|?[\s:\-|]+\|?\s*$',blines[1]) and '-' in blines[1]:
            continue
        if len(blines)==1:
            s0=blines[0].strip()
            nospace=s0.replace(' ','').replace('\t','')
            if len(nospace)>=3 and all(c==nospace[0] for c in nospace) and nospace[0] in ('*','-','_'):
                continue
        if len(blines)>=2 and blines[0].lstrip().startswith('```') and blines[-1].strip().startswith('```'):
            middle=blines[1:-1]
            ct=" ".join([l.strip() for l in middle])
            block_texts.append(ct.strip())
            continue
        is_ind2=True
        for ln in blines:
            if ln.strip()=="":
                continue
            if not ln.startswith('    '):
                is_ind2=False
                break
        if is_ind2 and len(blines)>=1:
            stripped=[ln[4:] if ln.startswith('    ') else ln for ln in blines]
            ct2=" ".join([l.strip() for l in stripped if l.strip()!=""])
            block_texts.append(ct2.strip())
            continue
        cleaned=[]
        for ln in blines:
            ln2=re.sub(r'^ {0,3}#{1,6}\s+','',ln)
            ln2=re.sub(r'^\s*>\s?','',ln2)
            ln2=re.sub(r'^\s*[-*+]\s+','',ln2)
            ln2=re.sub(r'^\s*\d+[.)]\s+','',ln2)
            ln2=re.sub(r'^\[[ xX]\]\s+','',ln2)
            cleaned.append(ln2)
        if len(cleaned)==2 and cleaned[1].lstrip().startswith(':'):
            term=cleaned[0].strip()
            defi=re.sub(r'^:\s*','',cleaned[1].strip())
            block_joined=term+defi
        else:
            block_joined=" ".join([l.strip() for l in cleaned])
        t=block_joined
        t=re.sub(r'!\[[^\]]*?\]\([^\)]+?\)','',t)
        t=re.sub(r'\[([^\]]*?)\]\([^\)]+?\)',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'`([^`\n]+?)`',r'\1',t)
        sup_en=options.get('crowbook.markdown.superscript',False)
        if sup_en:
            t=re.sub(r'~~([^~\n]+?)~~',r'\1',t)
            t=re.sub(r'~([^~\n]+?)~',r'\1',t)
            t=re.sub(r'\^([^\^\n]+?)\^',r'\1',t)
        else:
            t=re.sub(r'~~([^~\n]+?)~~',r'\1',t)
            t=re.sub(r'~([^~\n]+?)~',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'\*\*([^\*\n]+?)\*\*',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'__([^_\n]+?)__',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'\*([^\*\n]+?)\*',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'_([^_\n]+?)_',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'<((?:https?://|ftp://)[^<>\s]+?)>',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'\\(.)',r'\1',t)
        t=re.sub(r'\[\^([^\]]+?)\]','',t)
        block_texts.append(t)
    joined="".join(block_texts)
    chars=len(joined)
    words=len(joined.split()) if joined.strip()!="" else 0
    return chars,words

def format_stats(file_stats, total_chars, total_words):
    max_fn=max([len(fn) for fn,_,_ in file_stats]) if file_stats else 0
    header="Chapter"+" "*max_fn+"Chars      Words  Chars/Word"
    lines=[header,"---------"]
    for fn,ch,wo in file_stats:
        if wo==0:
            avg_str="NaN" if ch==0 else "inf"
        else:
            avg_str=f"{ch/wo:.2f}"
        gap1=11-(len(str(ch))-1)+(max_fn-len(fn))
        gap2=10-(len(str(wo))-1)
        gap3=8-(len(avg_str)-4)
        gap1=max(1,gap1); gap2=max(1,gap2); gap3=max(1,gap3)
        lines.append(f"{fn}{' '*gap1}{ch}{' '*gap2}{wo}{' '*gap3}{avg_str}")
    lines.append("---------")
    if total_words==0:
        total_avg="NaN" if total_chars==0 else "inf"
    else:
        total_avg=f"{total_chars/total_words:.2f}"
    gap1_t=11-(len(str(total_chars))-1)+(max_fn-len("TOTAL:"))
    gap2_t=10-(len(str(total_words))-1)
    gap3_t=8-(len(total_avg)-4)
    gap1_t=max(1,gap1_t); gap2_t=max(1,gap2_t); gap3_t=max(1,gap3_t)
    lines.append(f"TOTAL:{' '*gap1_t}{total_chars}{' '*gap2_t}{total_words}{' '*gap3_t}{total_avg}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)
